name: Kenosha Pass
notes: Ascends through dense, iconic golden aspen groves and lodgepole pines along the gentle eastern grade of Kenosha Pass in the Pike National Forest. The crest at 10,423 feet delivers breathtaking sweeping panoramas across the vast high-altitude prairie of the South Park basin. Cyclists and hikers find an accessible, flowing dirt doubletrack climb that serves as the premier gateway into the Continental Divide high country.
parkName: Pike National Forest

name: Georgia Pass
notes: Follows the historic 1860s gold-rush wagon road up Jefferson Creek before breaking through the subalpine spruce into alpine tundra on the Continental Divide. Towering directly overhead, the dramatic pyramidal horn of Mount Guyot dominates the skyline as you summit at 11,877 feet. Bikepackers face loose shale switchbacks and thin air above treeline, rewarded by a world-class, rowdy singletrack descent down the Swan River drainage into Summit County.
parkName: Pike National Forest / White River National Forest

name: Swan River Saddle
notes: Climbs out of the Middle Fork Swan River drainage on a steep, rocky forest doubletrack cutting between Keystone Gulch and the Swan River valley. Gradients ramp over 15% across loose mining talus and embedded granite boulders before topping out at 11,171 feet beneath Keystone Mountain. Riders should maintain steady seated traction to conquer the rocky churn before enjoying rolling, forested bench-cut singletrack toward Breckenridge.
parkName: White River National Forest

name: Tenmile Range Ridge (Peak 6)
notes: A brutal, legendary ascent out of Frisco up Miners Creek that relentlessly pushes riders through technical root-infested forest onto the exposed scree of the Tenmile Range. Breaching treeline onto the alpine crest beneath Peak 6 at 12,500 feet, travelers confront ferocious crosswinds and dizzying 360-degree vistas across the Gore Range and Breckenridge ski basins. The final pitch features punishing 20%+ pitches demanding supreme high-altitude grit, followed by a dizzying, switchbacking singletrack drop into Copper Mountain.
parkName: White River National Forest

name: Searles Pass
notes: Gradually ascends the alpine bench of Guller Creek above Copper Mountain through stunted spruce and willow flats onto the exposed saddle of Searles Pass at 12,047 feet. The trail contours along high-altitude tundra with sweeping views of Jacque Peak and the historic Camp Hale basin below. Early-season travelers must navigate stubborn snow drifts, while loose shale and high elevation demand measured pacing before pushing onward to neighboring Kokomo Pass.
parkName: White River National Forest

name: Kokomo Pass
notes: A soaring alpine traverse linking Searles Pass to Kokomo Pass across wide-open, wind-scoured Continental Divide tundra at 12,270 feet. The summit overlooks the historic World War II training valleys of Camp Hale and the rugged Gore Range wilderness to the north. Treacherous afternoon lightning storms require early crossings, followed by a sublime, flowing singletrack descent through Cataract Creek toward the Eagle River.
parkName: White River National Forest
landmark: Camp Hale National Monument / Elk Ridge

name: Tennessee Pass
notes: Traces the historic military training terrain of Camp Hale and old railroad grades up to the Continental Divide crossing at Tennessee Pass. The 5.8-mile climb follows gentle, pine-canopied doubletrack and smooth packed gravel with punchy switchbacks approaching Ski Cooper at 10,374 feet. It marks the transition from the Eagle River drainage into the storied high-altitude Leadville mining district and Sawatch Range.
parkName: San Isabel National Forest / White River National Forest

name: Mount Massive Timberline Bench
notes: Rolls along the scenic, pine-carpeted bench directly beneath the colossal eastern flank of Mount Massive, Colorado second-highest fourteen-thousand-foot peak. The trail hugs the shoreline ridges of Turquoise Lake on fast-rolling singletrack punctuated by granite root staircases and crystalline creek crossings. Riders enjoy gentle sustained grades and cool evergreen shade before approaching the bustling trailheads of Mount Elbert.
parkName: San Isabel National Forest / Mount Massive Wilderness

name: Lake Creek Saddle
notes: Ascends the forested moraine ridges dividing Halfmoon Creek and Lake Creek on the southeastern apron of Mount Elbert. The trail features technical granite rock gardens and tight switchbacks that test climbing finesse before topping out at 9,928 feet. The crest opens to spectacular views of the azure Twin Lakes shimmering below the towering pyramid of Mount Hope, leading into a fast, dusty singletrack descent into the historic village.
parkName: San Isabel National Forest

name: Mount Yale Flank
notes: Traverses the rugged, decomposed-granite slopes along the eastern foothills of 14,196-foot Mount Yale in the Collegiate Peaks Wilderness. A grueling 10.6-mile grind tests endurance with punchy roller-coaster climbs across dry pinon-juniper benches and high aspen glades overlooking the Upper Arkansas Valley. Water sources can be sparse along this sun-exposed segment, making proper hydration management vital before descending toward Cottonwood Hot Springs.
parkName: San Isabel National Forest / Collegiate Peaks Wilderness

name: Mount Shavano Flank
notes: Climbs sharply out of the dramatic Chalk Creek canyon on tight, rocky singletrack hugging the forested southern apron of Mount Shavano. Bikepackers encounter chunky granite ledges and technical root steps as they ascend past the iconic snow-formed Angel of Shavano toward 10,167 feet. The climb requires sustained power across loose talus benches, offering panoramic views of the Arkansas Valley and Mount Antero across the canyon.
parkName: San Isabel National Forest

name: Monarch Crest Trail
notes: A world-renowned epic climb ascending over 3,100 vertical feet along Fooses Creek to intersect the storied Continental Divide trail atop Monarch Ridge at 11,929 feet. The route transitions from lush streamside spruce into punishing, oxygen-starved rocky switchbacks and wide-open alpine scree. Exposed ridgeline riding offers breathtaking vistas across the San Luis Valley and Sawatch 14ers, though riders must heed notorious midday lightning strikes.
parkName: San Isabel National Forest / Gunnison National Forest

name: Marshall Pass Saddle
notes: A short, sharp crest following the historic Denver and Rio Grande narrow-gauge railroad corridor over the Continental Divide at 10,899 feet. Flanked by the southern bulk of Mount Ouray, this smooth gravel pass provides a brief respite and key junction for resupply toward Salida. It serves as the historic divide transition before plunging deeper south into the remote, desolate stretches of the Cochetopa Hills.
parkName: San Isabel National Forest / Gunnison National Forest

name: Sargents Mesa Crest
notes: The most infamous and mentally grueling sector of the entire Colorado Trail, renowned for its relentless, energy-sapping fields of volcanic baby head rocks and fallen timber. Climbing across the high divide plateau at 11,772 feet, travelers endure bone-rattling churn with virtually zero flow, compounded by an utter absence of dependable water sources for over twenty miles. Conquering Sargents Mesa demands unwavering psychological stamina, robust tubeless tire setups, and conservative hydration planning.
parkName: Gunnison National Forest / Rio Grande National Forest

name: Cochetopa Pass
notes: Climbs gently through expansive sagebrush valleys and open ponderosa forest along the historic Ute passage between the Gunnison River and San Luis basins. The 3.1-mile ascent features rolling dirt singletrack and doubletrack topping out at 10,256 feet near North Cochetopa Pass. Riders enjoy sweeping, wide-open western skies and relaxed grades, offering welcome relief after the punishing volcanic boulders of Sargents Mesa.
parkName: Gunnison National Forest

name: Los Pinos Divide
notes: An expansive 18.7-mile wilderness ascent traversing rolling sagebrush meadows and aspen draws above the meandering Cebolla Creek drainage in the northern San Juan foothills. Reaching 10,502 feet on Los Pinos Divide, the trail skirts the wild borders of the La Garita Wilderness with distant silhouettes of 14,014-foot San Luis Peak. The long, gradual climb demands steady aerobic pacing on remote doubletrack and bench-cut singletrack where elk herds frequently outnumber humans.
parkName: Gunnison National Forest / La Garita Wilderness
landmark: Cebolla Creek Valley / San Luis Peak

name: Spring Creek Pass Saddle
notes: A punchy, steep gravel rise crossing Colorado Highway 149 at 11,286 feet before launching into the formidable high alpine wilderness of the San Juan Mountains. Spring Creek Pass serves as a critical resupply and bailout access point near historic Lake City and the legendary Slumgullion Earthflow. From this wind-whipped saddle, travelers leave motorized corridors behind to begin the monumental, high-altitude climb toward Snow Mesa and Coney Summit.
parkName: Gunnison National Forest / Rio Grande National Forest

name: Coney Summit (Colorado Trail High Point)
notes: The crown jewel and highest physical point of the entire 567-mile Colorado Trail, cresting the wind-swept alpine tundra of the San Juan Mountains at an awe-inspiring 13,271 feet (4,045 m). Traversing the vast, treeless expanse of Snow Mesa beneath the jagged obelisk of the Rio Grande Pyramid, travelers endure hyperventilating climbs across loose volcanic talus and sharp tundra switchbacks. Exposure to violent electrical storms and sudden blizzards is acute; early morning ascents and relentless weather vigilance are essential for survival on this stratospheric divide.
parkName: Rio Grande National Forest / Weminuche Wilderness

name: Stony Pass Saddle
notes: A rugged alpine climb across the Continental Divide near the historic 1870s stagecoach freight road that originally linked Del Norte to the Silverton mining camps. Ascending across rocky talus fields beneath the towering crags of Canby Mountain, the trail reaches 12,986 feet near the infant headwaters of the Rio Grande. Severe weather, loose shale footing, and thin mountain air challenge every pedal stroke, rewarded by spectacular vistas down Cunningham Gulch.
parkName: San Juan National Forest / Weminuche Wilderness
landmark: Rio Grande River Headwaters / Canby Mountain

name: Molas Pass Ridge
notes: A punishing, sustained 2,280-foot singletrack grunt climbing out of the deep Animas River canyon alongside the historic Durango and Silverton Narrow Gauge Railroad. The trail relentlessly switchbacks up steep spruce-fir slopes, featuring technical rock steps and loose decomposing shale before topping out at Molas Pass (11,549 ft). Cyclists and hikers are treated to heart-stopping panoramas across the Animas gorge toward the jagged spires of the Grenadier and Needle ranges.
parkName: San Juan National Forest / Weminuche Wilderness

name: Blackhawk Pass
notes: A steep, breathtaking alpine staircase that punches through lush wildflower meadows and subalpine cirques in the Hermosa Creek headwaters. With grades averaging over 9% and ramping to 17% across exposed switchbacks, riders must exert intense anaerobic power to crest the razor ridge at 11,995 feet. The summit presents stunning, layered views of Blackhawk Mountain and the distant red amphitheaters of the Lizard Head Wilderness.
parkName: San Juan National Forest / Hermosa Creek Wilderness

name: Kennebec Pass (Indian Trail Ridge)
notes: The grand alpine finale of the Colorado Trail, executing an exhilarating 11.8-mile ridgeline traverse along the knife-edge crest of Indian Trail Ridge to Kennebec Pass at 12,287 feet. Perched high in the jagged La Plata Mountains, this technical singletrack demands supreme bike-handling over loose shattered scree, exposed ledges, and steep tundra drop-offs. The summit marks the gateway to the celebrated, uninterrupted 20-mile, 5,000-foot descent down Junction Creek directly to the southern terminus in Durango.
parkName: San Juan National Forest
